comment: Design-contract ratchet for Exo's stylesheet, ported from obsidian-cosmos-theme/contract.sh + design-contract.json (2026-08-11, the Cosmos Bridge wave). Numbers may only go DOWN, or stay equal. Raising one is not a bump: it is a new audit verdict, and it belongs in docs/2026-07-mv-kit-audit.md with a motivation, the way every survivor below already is.
important_max_comment: The six survivors of the 2026-07 mv-kit audit, each with a written verdict: 1 hover-over-the-close-button opacity (waived), 3 inside the blanket prefers-reduced-motion block (pass: accessibility overrides are the canonical sanctioned use), 2 on the keyboard focus ring, which Obsidian core and several themes would otherwise strip (waived, same accessibility class). Enumerated line by line in src/style-contract.test.ts.
raw_hex_comment: Raw colour hexes in styles.css, comments stripped. Four, and each is the ONLY copy of itself: three semantic status fallbacks declared once in the seam (--mva-ok / --mva-caution / --mva-danger), plus the artifact iframe's `background: #fff`, waived by the audit as document paper rather than a Cosmos surface (hex group 11). This was 49 until 2026-08-12. The other 45 were the same three colours retyped at 43 call sites via the `var(--color-x, #fallback)` recipe, plus four dead fallbacks on Obsidian vars that Obsidian always defines. The recipe was never wrong, the repetition was: `.mva-conn-dot.is-failed` had drifted to a fourth orange (#e0a458) that no other rule used, which is precisely the failure a single declaration makes impossible. The two provider brand accents are NOT here: they live in the provider adapters as `brandColor` and are applied to identity dots from TypeScript, never as a fill in this file. The assertion `§3 provider brand colours never appear in the stylesheet as brand fills` reads both hexes straight out of the adapters, so that collision cannot come back quietly.
